F071 / provisional KI#393 — MULTI-UNIT BOMBARD PREVIEWS COUNT INELIGIBLE UNITS

CvDLLWidgetData.cpp MISSION_BOMBARD help (current ~2914):
  for each UI-selected unit:
      iDamage += kSelectedUnit.damageToBombardTarget(kMissionPlot);

The preview does not require kSelectedUnit.canMove() or
kSelectedUnit.canBombard(kMissionPlot). By contrast, actual execution in
CvSelectionGroup::startMission repeatedly calls
AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD), and that helper explicitly skips units
that cannot move or fail canBombard(kAt).

Reachable example: a selected siege group contains one fresh siege unit and one
unit that has already spent its attack/bombard for the turn. At least one unit
can still bombard, so the action remains available. The tooltip sums nominal
damage from both; execution skips the spent unit. The preview can therefore
promise more city-defense reduction than the mission can deliver.

Sibling in CvGameTextMgr::getAirBombPlotHelp:
  - the helper first establishes that one best unit can air-bomb the hovered
    target;
  - for revealed city targets it then loops over every selected unit and adds
    airBombDefenseDamage without checking canMove/canAirBombAt(target).
Thus a fresh eligible aircraft plus an exhausted or out-of-range selected
companion can similarly overstate city-defense damage.

Concrete SAS XML range control: Fighter range 6 / bomb rate 8; Bomber range 8 /
bomb rate 16; Jet Fighter range 10 / bomb rate 12; Stealth Bomber range 12 /
bomb rate 20; Guided Missile range 5 / bomb rate 16. For a city 7 tiles away,
a Bomber can be valid while a selected Fighter is out of range; once the valid
best-unit gate passes, the city preview still adds the Fighter's nominal
airBombDefenseDamage.

Ancestry: the ground and air multi-unit previews were introduced together in
AdvCiv practical 2778 / commit 4098fbb24851e4cdc6f2f615f4458adedf97da75,
"Various UI improvements for bombard and air bomb missions." The same commit
also added per-unit eligibility-aware execution, making the omitted tooltip
filters especially clear.

Conservative repair direction:
  - ground preview: add damage only for units that can move and
    canBombard(kMissionPlot) (or otherwise mirror the actual mission selector);
  - air-city preview: add damage only for units that can move and
    canAirBombAt(kPlot).
Do not merely test bombard/air-bomb base rate: target/move-state eligibility is
the mismatch.

F072 / provisional KI#394 — AIR BOMB BEST-UNIT SELECTION CAN ABORT A VALID GROUP ORDER

Current CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_AIRBOMB, pMissionPlot):
  - common loop filters !pUnit->canMove();
  - city branch tests pUnit->canAirBomb(pMissionPlot), NOT canAirBombAt;
  - CvUnit::canAirBomb's pFrom parameter is explicitly unused and it tests only
    generic air-bomb ability / attack-spent state;
  - non-city branch has no target-eligibility test at all.

Actual group execution in CvSelectionGroup::startMission is:
  while ((pUnit = AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_AIRBOMB, &kMissionPlot)) != NULL &&
         pUnit->airBomb(kMissionPlot, ...))
      ...
CvUnit::airBomb begins with canAirBombAt(kTarget) and returns false if the chosen
unit cannot attack that target. Because the while condition then fails, the
mission loop stops instead of trying another eligible selected aircraft.

CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_AIRBOMB) proves normal reachability:
it returns true if ANY selected unit canAirBombAt(target), so invalid companion
units are allowed to remain in a group whose Air Bomb order is valid.

Concrete current-SAS example from CIV4UnitInfos.xml:
  UNIT_BOMBER: iBombRate=16, iAirRange=8, cost=180
  UNIT_JET_FIGHTER: iBombRate=12, iAirRange=10, cost=170
Against a city 9 tiles away, the Jet Fighter is target-valid and makes the
mission available; the Bomber is out of range. City prioritization nevertheless
uses nominal airBombDefenseDamage and can prefer the higher-rate Bomber. The
chosen Bomber's airBomb(target) then rejects range 9 and the while loop stops,
so the valid Jet Fighter never acts. The same eligibility omission exists for
non-city air-bomb targets.

Ancestry:
  - practical 2778 / 4098fbb248... introduced the smarter grouped Air Bomb
    ordering with the same generic canAirBomb test for city targets and no
    target filter in the non-city ordering;
  - practical 2784 / 160fa499a896cf595f74bcbde68b7ce41bedc466 factored the
    ordering into CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission and preserved the
    missing target-eligibility check exactly;
  - later bombard-priority work (e.g. practical 2809) retained it.

Conservative repair direction: in MISSION_AIRBOMB selection, reject any unit
that does not pUnit->canAirBombAt(*pMissionPlot) (using the proper current
signature/origin semantics) before ranking it. That aligns selection with
canDoMission, CvUnit::airBomb, and the target-specific mission contract.

F071 PARADROP SIBLING (ADDED AFTER WIP09)
CvGameTextMgr::getParadropPlotHelp chooses the selected unit with the greatest
interception-evasion value before applying target/move eligibility. It then
emits interception help only if that chosen unit canParadropAt the target.

This differs from actual group execution: CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission
(MISSION_PARADROP) first requires canMove and canParadropAt(target), then ranks
eligible units. Current SAS has UNIT_PARATROOPER with equal drop/evasion stats,
so a normal mixed-move-state selection is enough: one tied Paratrooper has
already moved, another is fresh. The fresh unit keeps the Paradrop order valid
and is the unit execution can use, but the help loop can retain the moved tied
unit and then suppress interception information when its final canParadropAt
check fails.

This is normalized under F071 because its cause and repair principle are the
same as the already-recorded Ground Bombard and Air Bomb preview cases: first
restrict the help population to mission-executable units at the target, then
aggregate/rank them. Do not create a separate finding merely for each mission.

REJECTED F073 CANDIDATE — MISSION_HEAL MAX_INT IS SEMANTICALLY REAL
parseActionHelp_Mission computes the group Heal ETA as the maximum healTurns()
of all selected units, and CvUnit::healTurns returns MAX_INT when a hurt unit's
net heal rate at the plot is <= 0. At first this looked like another raw sentinel
leak.

Engine semantics show otherwise:
- CvUnit::canHeal rejects healTurns()==MAX_INT, so such a unit alone cannot make
  the Heal mission available.
- If another selected unit can heal, the group can nevertheless enter
  ACTIVITY_HEAL.
- CvUnit::doTurn applies feature turn-damage and then doHeal to hurt stationary
  units; the group remains ACTIVITY_HEAL while any member remains hurt (for a
  human group, absent the separate sentry-danger wake condition).
- Therefore a hurt selected unit whose healing is exactly cancelled/exceeded by
  feature turn damage really can keep the group from ever becoming fully healed
  at that plot. MAX_INT is meaningful as an infinite group ETA in that state,
  not a finite-production-style sentinel masquerading as ordinary data.

Result: reject this candidate. F073 stays unused.

- executeAction likewise calls doMenu() and then falls through to doConscript(). This shape is inherited and also present in the local controls.

F076 / provisional KI#398 — group Espionage can abort a valid order by trying the first movable non-Spy
Status: NEW INHERITED BTS GAMEPLAY / GROUP-MISSION CONTRACT DEFECT ROOT; current SAS reproduction and vanilla/BtS control proof strong.

Mission-availability contract:
- CvGame::canHandleAction delegates mission legality to the selected interface group's canStartMission.
- CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_ESPIONAGE) iterates the group and returns true when ANY unit satisfies canEspionage(target, bTestVisible) and, when required, canMove().
- Therefore a mixed same-domain group legitimately exposes/enables Espionage when one selected Spy can act, even if other selected units cannot.

Execution contract failure:
- CvSelectionGroup::startMission iterates units in group order, skipping only units that cannot move.
- MISSION_ESPIONAGE calls pUnit->espionage(...) on the first movable unit it reaches and then unconditionally jumps to exit_unit_loop, explicitly to allow one unit at a time to do espionage.
- CvUnit::espionage immediately returns false when canEspionage(plot()) is false; CvUnit::canEspionage rejects every non-Spy through !isSpy().
- Consequently the executor stops after a failed attempt by an ineligible movable unit rather than continuing until it reaches the Spy that made the group mission legal.

Concrete current SAS reproduction:
- CvUnit::canJoinGroup allows same-owner units on the same plot to group when their domains match; it does not forbid Spy + combat-unit groups.
- Current UNIT_AXEMAN is DOMAIN_LAND, DefaultUnitAI=UNITAI_ATTACK, bSpy=0.
- Current UNIT_SPY is DOMAIN_LAND, DefaultUnitAI=UNITAI_SPY, bSpy=1.
- CvSelectionGroup::addUnit orders units by AI_groupFirstVal (then second value). UNITAI_ATTACK has first value 13; UNITAI_SPY has 9. Thus a normal Axeman + Spy group deterministically puts the Axeman before the Spy.
- On a rival-owned plot where the fresh Spy is legally able to perform espionage and the fresh Axeman can move, canDoMission returns true because of the Spy.
- startMission reaches the Axeman first; Axeman::espionage returns false because it is not a Spy; the unconditional exit prevents the eligible Spy from acting. A valid Espionage order can therefore produce no espionage action/popup.

Help sibling:
- parseActionHelp_Mission(MISSION_ESPIONAGE) uses the head selected unit kUnit and passes only that unit to setEspionageMissionHelp.
- setEspionageMissionHelp immediately returns for !isSpy(). In the same Axeman + Spy ordering, the action is enabled by the Spy but Spy-specific mission help is omitted because the head is the Axeman.
- This reinforces the same group-selection assumption, though the executor failure is independently sufficient for F076.

Ancestry/control:
- The local Civ4CE BtS source has the same contract split: canDoMission iterates until any pLoopUnit->canEspionage succeeds, while execution attempts espionage on the current loop unit and then sets pUnitNode=NULL regardless of success to stop after one unit.
- The AdvCiv/SAS goto exit_unit_loop is a readability/control-flow rewrite of that inherited BtS behavior, not the birth of the defect.

Conservative repair direction:
- Preserve the "one Spy per Espionage command" rule, but exit the unit loop only after selecting/attempting an actually eligible Spy.
- With canMove already filtered by the outer loop, the MISSION_ESPIONAGE case can continue past units that fail canEspionage(plot()) and stop after the first eligible Spy performs/opens the espionage action.
- Keep the two-phase/popup semantics intact; do not allow multiple Spies to execute one user command.
- For help, derive the espionage-help subject from an eligible selected Spy rather than blindly from the group head.

- Generic enum casts without reachable bad widget producers remain non-findings; theoretical forged payloads are not being promoted.
- WIDGET_EXAMINE_CITY's direct city lookup remains protected by ordinary live-owned-city callers; no supported stale-city path has been proven.
- parseTradeRoutes' player IDs remain valid across all live callers inspected.

- MISSION_BUILD worker ETA does not double-count workers already performing the same build: getBuildTurnsLeft accounts for active builders while widget help adds selected workers only when their current build differs.

RESUMED NORMALIZATION — F071 / provisional KI#393 BROADENED
F071's causal family is now stronger than the previously recorded Ground Bombard,
Air Bomb and Paradrop cases. Additional current-SAS mixed-selection reproductions
show that parseActionHelp_Mission sometimes derives mission help from the head
selected unit rather than from the unit(s) that actually make the group mission
executable:

1) MISSION_LEAD / Lead Troops
- A normal Axeman + Great General land group can be ordered with the Axeman first:
  UNITAI_ATTACK has group-first priority 13, while UNITAI_GREAT_GENERAL has 11.
- The Great General makes Lead valid, but the help path receives the head Axeman.
- The General-specific +20 XP / Leader-promotion explanation can therefore be
  omitted even though the selected group can execute Lead.

2) MISSION_DISCOVER
- A normal Axeman + Great Scientist group can have the Axeman as head.
- The main discovery-value calculation searches the selected units and can find
  the Scientist correctly, but the later discovery-path helper receives the head
  Axeman's UnitTypes value.
- The Axeman has no discovery flavor/base discovery role, so the actual Great
  Scientist bulb-path explanation can disappear from an otherwise valid action.

3) MISSION_PLUNDER
- Current UNIT_TRANSPORT uses UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA (group-first 11) and bPillage=0.
- Current UNIT_DESTROYER uses UNITAI_RESERVE_SEA (group-first 2) and bPillage=1.
- In a Transport + Destroyer selection, the Destroyer can make Plunder/Blockade
  legal while the Transport remains the group head.
- Head-unit-only help can then emit the non-plundering unit's refusal/diagnostic
  text despite another selected unit being the actual executable subject.

Normalization: keep these under F071, not separate IDs. The common repair rule is
to derive special-mission help from the same eligibility population that can
execute the selected mission, then aggregate/rank only those eligible units.

F076 / provisional KI#398 — REPAIR MODEL DEEPENED
The WIP14 executor proof remains valid: a mixed Axeman + Spy group can expose
Espionage because the Spy passes canDoMission, then startMission reaches the
movable Axeman first, calls espionage(), receives false because it is not a Spy,
and exits before reaching the eligible Spy.

A naive repair of only that unit loop is NOT sufficient. The two-phase popup flow
also loses the acting Spy identity:
- CvUnit::espionage(NO_ESPIONAGEMISSION) queues BUTTONPOPUP_DOESPIONAGE without
  storing the invoking Spy ID.
- CvDLLButtonPopup::launchDoEspionagePopup later calls getHeadSelectedUnit() and
  uses that unit to test/build available espionage missions.
- In the concrete Axeman + Spy ordering, the head is still the Axeman; K-Mod's
  canDoEspionageMission path rejects the non-Spy, so a merely loop-fixed command
  can still open an empty/Cancel-only mission popup.
- launchDoEspionageTargetPopup likewise reacquires getHeadSelectedUnit() for the
  acting Spy; parseEspionageCostHelp also follows the head-selection identity.
- Popup return messages push the selection-group mission and do not carry a Spy
  unit ID that would repair this identity loss downstream.

Repair implication: F076 is an end-to-end selected-actor identity problem, not
only a missing `continue` in startMission. Preserve one-Spy-per-command and the

F077 / provisional KI#399 — INHERITED BTS GREAT-GENERAL XP REMAINDER CAN BE LOST
Status: strong inherited gameplay/mechanics defect discovered while following
MISSION_LEAD help/execution from the open CvDLLWidgetData audit.

Current code contract
CvUnit::giveExperience():
1. canGiveExperience(plot) counts only eligible own units other than the Warlord.
2. getStackExperienceToGive(iNumUnits) computes a total XP pool from that eligible
   count.
3. iMinExperiencePerUnit = total / eligible count and iRemainder = total % count.
4. The award loop correctly grants XP only when:
      pUnit != this && same owner && pUnit->canAcquirePromotionAny()
   BUT the remainder index `i` is incremented outside that eligibility block.

Consequently every ineligible plot-list entry consumes a position in the
`i < iRemainder` test despite receiving no XP. The intended remainder points can
therefore disappear rather than being assigned to eligible recipients.

Concrete current-SAS reproduction without any exotic stack
- UNIT_GREAT_GENERAL has iLeaderExperience=20.
- Current GlobalDefinesAlt has WARLORD_EXTRA_EXPERIENCE_PER_UNIT_PERCENT=10 and
  WARLORD_MAXIMUM_EXTRA_EXPERIENCE_PERCENT=100.
- With 4 eligible recipients, getStackExperienceToGive computes:
      20 * (100 + (4-1)*10) / 100 = 26 XP.
  Intended split: 7 + 7 + 6 + 6 = 26.
- Current UnitTypes ordering places UNIT_GREAT_GENERAL at index 129 of 131;
  ordinary current combat recipients are lower UnitTypes (e.g. Axeman 30,
  Maceman 39, Rifleman 58, Infantry 61).
- CvPlot::addUnit orders same-owner/same-domain plot units through
  CvUnit::isBeforeUnitCycle; when unit types differ, higher UnitTypes come first.
  Therefore the Great General itself normally precedes ordinary land recipients.
- The loop sees the General first: it is excluded from XP, but the unconditional
  `i++` changes i from 0 to 1. The four eligible recipients then see i=1,2,3,4.
  With iRemainder=2, only the first recipient satisfies i<2. Actual award becomes
  7+6+6+6 = 25 XP: 1 XP silently vanishes.
- Additional ineligible units ordered before recipients (for example another
  non-recipient) can consume still more remainder positions. No such extra unit
  is required for the basic defect because the Warlord itself already does so.

Why this is not merely a tooltip discrepancy
getStackExperienceToGive returns the intended pool, and canGiveExperience supplies
its eligible denominator. The award loop then fails to distribute that pool.
This affects real unit experience and promotion progression. MISSION_LEAD help
can additionally advertise the nominal pool, but the mechanics loss is the
independent root and is sufficient for F077.

Ancestry/control
- AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same unconditional `i++` outside the eligibility block.
- The supplied Civ4CE/BtS implementation has the same structure, including the
  unconditional increment after each plot unit. This establishes the defect as
  inherited BtS behavior rather than an AdvCiv-SAS regression.
- K-Mod/AdvCiv increased Warlord scaling, which changes when/how much remainder
  exists, but did not introduce the indexing mistake itself.

Conservative repair direction
Advance the remainder-distribution index only when an eligible unit actually
receives experience, e.g. move `i++` into the eligibility branch after the award
(or use an explicitly named `iEligibleRecipient`). This preserves plot iteration
order and all existing total-XP/scaling rules while guaranteeing that exactly
`iRemainder` eligible recipients receive the +1 point.

NORMALIZATION NOTE
F077 is cross-file (CvUnit.cpp), but it was source-reached directly through the
CvDLLWidgetData MISSION_LEAD contract audit. Prior album findings already retain
cross-caller/executor roots when they are necessary to explain the widget-visible
behavior (e.g. F067/F072/F076), so preserving it here is consistent and useful.
It should also be carried into the eventual CvUnit.cpp audit as an already-known
root rather than rediscovered/double-counted there.

F071 / provisional KI#393 -- RETAINED AFTER FINAL ADVERSARIAL REVIEW
Multi-unit mission help can describe/rank/aggregate the selection head or all
selected units instead of the subset that can actually execute the hovered
mission. Proven siblings remain:
- Ground Bombard can sum nominal bombard damage from spent/ineligible selected
  siege units while execution filters through canBombard.
- Air Bomb help can analogously overcount aircraft that cannot execute at the
  target.
- Paradrop interception help can select a moved/high-evasion or tied unit and
  suppress information although another selected Paratrooper can execute.
- Lead Troops help can use an ordinary combat head unit even when a selected
  Great General makes the action executable, omitting the General-specific XP /
  leader-promotion details.
- Discover computes the main bulb amount through an eligible unit search but
  later calls setDiscoverPathHelp with the selection-head unit type, so the path
  explanation can disappear in a mixed selection.
- Plunder/blockade can be executable through a selected pillaging naval unit
  while a non-plundering head unit supplies a false inability diagnostic.
MISSION_PILLAGE and Corporation Spread were explicitly challenged and rejected as
additional siblings; they are not needed to support this root.

F072 / provisional KI#394 -- RETAINED AFTER FINAL ADVERSARIAL REVIEW
AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_AIRBOMB) does not consistently filter candidates by
target eligibility. For city targets it uses generic canAirBomb rather than
canAirBombAt; for non-city targets it can likewise rank without the target test.
A chosen out-of-range/ineligible aircraft can then fail CvUnit::airBomb and stop
the group mission before a valid selected companion acts. The current SAS
Bomber-range-8 / Jet-Fighter-range-10 example against a city at distance 9
remains a concrete reproduction family.

The BUG/AdvCiv Chevron angry-citizen overlay places a hit-testable DDS over the

F076 / KI#398 -- RETAINED AND REPAIR SCOPE DEEPENED
Mixed-group Espionage can be enabled by a selected Spy while
CvSelectionGroup::startMission reaches a movable non-Spy first, calls its

Furthermore a naive repair that merely skips non-Spies is insufficient:
BUTTONPOPUP_DOESPIONAGE does not retain the acting Spy ID, and both espionage
popup phases return to getHeadSelectedUnit(). The actor identity must survive the
whole popup/return path. Lead Troops is a strong local negative control: its
popup explicitly stores the Great General's unit ID and resolves that stored
actor later, demonstrating the appropriate engine pattern.

F077 / KI#399 -- RETAINED CROSS-FILE ROOT (CvUnit.cpp)
CvUnit::giveExperience correctly calculates Great-General total XP and remainder
from eligible recipients, but increments its remainder-distribution index for
every plot unit, including units that receive no XP. Ineligible entries therefore
consume remainder slots and silently destroy intended experience.

The ordinary current-SAS four-recipient reproduction remains deterministic:
20 base leader XP with current Warlord scaling yields 26 intended XP, nominally
7+7+6+6. Same-owner/same-domain plot ordering places the high-UnitTypes Great
General before ordinary land recipients; the General is excluded from the award
but still consumes the first unconditional index increment, producing 7+6+6+6
= 25 actual XP. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and Civ4CE/BtS preserve the same inherited loop
shape. Repair direction remains to advance the remainder index only when XP is
actually awarded to an eligible recipient.

F077 is a post-C007 cross-file amendment reached through MISSION_LEAD during this
widget audit. CvUnit.cpp was already durably audited earlier; do not rediscover or
double-count this root later merely because implementation review returns to
CvUnit.cpp.

produced several source-proven directional-state defects (KI#369/KI#370). The
method was treated as a state migration: enumerate team-indexed and transient
team state, then prove whether both the survivor->outsider and outsider->survivor
directions retain semantically live values after absorbed players are reassigned.

F078 / provisional KI#400 -- inherited Permanent Alliance merge drops active
Counterespionage effects in both directions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATE / CONTRACT
- CvTeam owns two directional arrays:
  m_aiCounterespionageTurnsLeftAgainstTeam and
  m_aiCounterespionageModAgainstTeam.
- The live Counterespionage mission in current SAS has exactly one nonzero
  definition: 10 turns and +100 modifier. CvPlayer::doEspionageMission applies
  both values to the acting team's entry against the target team.
- Espionage mission cost reads the target team's Counterespionage modifier
  against the acting spy's current team. The effect is therefore keyed strictly
  by current TeamTypes identity, not by player identity.
- An active effect cannot normally be started again against the same target while
  its turns-left entry is positive, so each directional team pair represents one
  live effect rather than an arbitrary stack.

MERGE FAILURE
- shareCounters explicitly preserves neighboring temporary/history state such as
  StolenVisibilityTimer, WarWeariness and AI relation counters, but it never
  transfers either Counterespionage array from the absorbed team to the survivor.
- CvTeam::addTeam's reverse outsider-direction merge likewise combines
  StolenVisibilityTimer and EspionagePointsAgainstTeam but never combines the
  outsider's Counterespionage entries against the two constituent teams.
- After absorbed players change from team B to survivor A, entries keyed to B are
  unreachable for ordinary espionage cost calculations.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION
1. Team B performs Counterespionage against team C and has, e.g., 7 turns of the
   +100 effect remaining.
2. B enters a Permanent Alliance and is absorbed into A.
3. A had no corresponding effect against C.
4. Former B spies/territory now belong to team A, so all checks use A<->C.
5. B's still-positive B->C timer/modifier remain on the dead team entry and the
   +100 effect disappears immediately. The reverse C->B case is lost analogously.

CONTROL / ANCESTRY
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and the supplied Civ4CE/BtS source contain the same omission.
- Firaxis already preserves StolenVisibilityTimer in this exact merge family,
  making Counterespionage the conspicuous neighboring temporary espionage state
  that was not migrated.

REPAIR DIRECTION
- Preserve the live pair in both directions when team identities collapse.
- Current data has only the single +100 mission, so choosing the longer remaining
  active effect is unambiguous in practical SAS. Do not sum durations/modifiers.
- If future XML adds different Counterespionage modifiers, copy a coherent
  timer+modifier pair rather than independently manufacturing maxima.

Classification: inherited BtS/Firaxis defect retained by AdvCiv/SAS.


F079 / provisional KI#401 -- AdvCiv Permanent Alliance resets inherited
first-contact dates used by Info Screen graphs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATE / ORIGIN
- AdvCiv practical 2468 (f91c93bea834f12a3f5da1894d8afaa1a07b4cac,
  "Show score graph (Info screen) regardless of espionage") replaced the old
  boolean has-met state with m_aiHasMetTurn.
- makeHasMet records the current game turn in that array.
- CvInfoScreen uses getHasMetTurn to hide pre-contact score history and to gate
  partial score graphs for five turns after first contact.
- That introducing commit changed reset/serialization/makeHasMet and the Info
  Screen but did not update CvTeam::addTeam/shareCounters.

MERGE FAILURE
- addTeam propagates missing contacts by calling meet(eOther,false) before the
  absorbed players are reassigned.
- If B met C long ago but survivor A did not, A.meet(C) writes the alliance turn
  as A's new first-contact date; the reciprocal C->A entry is also written now.
- The old B<->C timestamps remain attached to the soon-dead B identity.
- Even when both constituent teams had met C, the merged team does not normalize
  the timestamp to the earliest inherited contact.
- The older AI_getHasMetCounter *is* merged, so the omission is specifically the
  later-added real timestamp used by the UI.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION
- B and C first meet on turn 50.
- A has never met C.
- A absorbs B through a Permanent Alliance on turn 100.
- A and C become known through addTeam, but both relevant new A<->C timestamps
  become 100 rather than inheriting 50.
- Info Screen graph history that should be available through the allied team's
  prior knowledge is hidden as if first contact occurred on turn 100, and the
  five-turn partial-graph delay is restarted.

REPAIR DIRECTION
- For each inherited known relation, preserve the earliest nonnegative constituent
  has-met turn in both directions. A missing (-1) value must not beat a real date.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv regression introduced when advc.091 added the
first-contact timestamp without extending Permanent Alliance state migration.


F080 / provisional KI#402 -- AdvCiv Permanent Alliance can leave a live
Disengage deal without its enforcement flag
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATE / ORIGIN
- AdvCiv practical 1285 (8aaaae059d3db7d47d430c099ace4adc92e3afdb,
  "Temporary right of passage after making peace") introduced TRADE_DISENGAGE and
  m_abDisengage.
- The trade is a dual player-to-player CvDeal, while actual movement/diplomacy
  enforcement uses directional CvTeam::isDisengage flags.
- Starting the trade sets the team flag; ending it clears the flag and may bump
  units from territory that is no longer friendly.

MERGE FAILURE
- CvDeal::isBetween(TeamTypes,TeamTypes) derives the teams dynamically from the
  deal's stored players via TEAMID.
- Therefore a live B<->C Disengage deal automatically becomes an A<->C deal when
  B's player is reassigned to survivor team A during addTeam.
- addTeam explicitly transfers Open Borders, Defensive Pact, Force Peace and other
  team relations, but never transfers m_abDisengage from B<->C to A<->C.
- The practical-1285 implementation did add TRADE_DISENGAGE to the list of deals
  canceled *between the two merging teams*; it did not address outsider deals.
- A B<->C outsider Disengage deal is not killed by that merged-team cleanup: after
  reassignment it is an A<->C deal, not an A<->A deal.

CONSEQUENCE
- The deal remains present and continues counting down, but the team-level flag
  that grants its temporary right of passage is false on A<->C unless A happened
  to have an independent effect.
- Unit/plot/diplomacy code querying isDisengage therefore stops honoring the still
  live deal. At eventual deal termination, endTrade operates on the players'
  *current* teams and clears A<->C, further demonstrating that the deal itself is
  considered migrated even though its enforcement state was not.

REPAIR DIRECTION
- When an absorbed team has a live Disengage relation with an outsider, migrate
  the corresponding team relation to survivor<->outsider (both directions as
  required by the dual trade), or deliberately cancel the surviving outsider deal
  and enforce that as a documented policy. Silently keeping the deal while losing
  its state is inconsistent.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv defect introduced with advc.034.


F081 / provisional KI#403 -- Permanent Alliance can erase an in-flight
spaceship launch / victory countdown
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATE / REACHABILITY
- Permanent Alliance trading has no condition prohibiting the trade after a team
  has launched a spaceship; the human path can therefore reach this normally.
- launch() stores the actual in-flight state in m_aiVictoryCountdown and clears
  canLaunch for that victory.
- shareCounters transfers spaceship ProjectCount state (using the established
  max-of-two-teams rule). changeProjectCount subsequently recomputes canLaunch
  from the merged project requirements.
- addTeam/shareCounters never transfer m_aiVictoryCountdown.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION
1. Team B launches and has 5 turns remaining before arrival.
2. B joins A via Permanent Alliance while the game is still running.
3. B's project/component counts are transferred to A.
4. B's countdown remains keyed to the dead B team and A retains its own default
   -1 (not launched) countdown.
5. The transferred projects can make A canLaunch again; the merged team has lost
   the existing ship-in-flight and must launch again from a fresh full delay (or
   can simply remain indefinitely in the not-launched state).

CONTROLS
- Current SAS, base AdvCiv 1.14 and supplied Civ4CE/BtS all omit countdown state
  from addTeam.
- CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE) checks team/vassal/war/
  member/trading conditions but does not reject a live victory countdown.

TWO-LAUNCH COLLISION / REPAIR DIRECTION
- The merged team has only one countdown slot per victory. If either constituent
  has a live countdown, preserve it; if both do, preserve the minimum nonnegative
  value (earliest arrival), which is the least destructive representation of two
  already-launched team victories.
- While a countdown is active, keep canLaunch false; transferred project counts
  must not silently re-enable a second launch.

Classification: inherited BtS/Firaxis Permanent Alliance state-migration defect.


NEGATIVE CONTROLS / NEIGHBORING STATE CHECKED SO FAR
----------------------------------------------------

- m_abHasSeen does not immediately justify another root: addTeam copies absorbed
  revealed-map/city information to the survivor and explicitly meets inherited
  contacts, both of which invoke the existing identity-seen machinery.
- m_abJustDeclaredWar is reset each turn and war synchronization in addTeam runs
  through ordinary declaration paths where a new declaration is actually needed;
  no independent persistent-state loss has been established.
- KI#369 SharedWarSuccess and KI#370 reverse OpenBordersCounter are already fixed
  in the authoritative practical-6252 tree and were used as controls, not
  rediscovered.
- m_aiTurnsAtPeace is already merged in both the own and outsider directions by
  advc.130k / the existing SAS fixes.
- EspionagePointsAgainstTeam and EspionagePointsEver are explicitly summed during
  the merge; no loss found there.

F081 / provisional KI#403 -- strengthening: even the SURVIVING launched team can
be made launchable again by the Permanent Alliance project transfer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The WIP01 root remains valid and is stronger than the absorbed-team reproduction
alone showed.

- CvPlayer::launch stores the in-flight state in m_aiVictoryCountdown and calls
  setCanLaunch(eVictory, false).
- shareCounters transfers a larger absorbed project count through
  changeProjectCount.
- changeProjectCount recomputes setCanLaunch(eVictory,
  GC.getGame().testVictory(eVictory, getID())) for every victory threshold touched.
- CvGame::testVictory checks the project/victory conditions but does not test an
  already-live victory countdown.

Therefore, if survivor A itself has already launched and B brings a higher count
of any victory-relevant spaceship component, the merge can set A.canLaunch back to
true while A's original countdown is still running. The problem is not only that
an absorbed B countdown is lost; transferred project state can also contradict a
survivor countdown already present.

Normalized repair requirement: after project counts have been merged, restore the
chosen live countdown (minimum nonnegative constituent countdown) and force
canLaunch=false for that victory whenever that countdown is active.


F082 / provisional KI#404 -- AdvCiv doubles the overflow portion in stored
completed-tech research progress
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
- AdvCiv practical 2082, commit 5a6bff0b8fbdb037f0c875aab7d3d6ed61beba09
  ("Some misc. refactoring") added the line while explicitly describing the work
  as cleaner/safer handling of research progress for already-discovered techs.
- The local source comment says: "Cleaner to subtract the overflow. Cf. comment in
  getResearchProgress."
- The adjacent getResearchProgress comment says that, once a tech is known, the
  stored value is the beakers the team put into it and can even be 0.

ACTUAL ARITHMETIC
Suppose the completion call has research progress P = C + O, where C is cost and
O is adjusted overflow. The code correctly grants player overflow from O, then:

    m_aiResearchProgress.add(eIndex,
        getResearchProgress(eIndex) - getResearchCost(eIndex));

EnumMap::add is ordinary arithmetic addition. Thus the stored value becomes:

    (C + O) + O = C + 2O

rather than subtracting O as the comment says. Vanilla/Civ4CE simply leaves the
old C+O value; this extra distortion is AdvCiv-specific.

REACHABILITY / IMPACT
- The wrong stored value is exposed through CyTeam::getResearchProgress and debug
  facilities.
- Most normal gameplay consumers first test isHasTech, which explains why this can
  remain quiet in ordinary play.
- Tech removal is nevertheless a supported engine operation (Advanced Start,
  regeneration/debug/WB-style paths use setHasTech(false)). Once a completed tech
  is removed, its stored progress becomes live research state again; an inflated
  >=cost value can therefore leak back into research/recompletion/overflow logic.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Subtract the adjusted overflow portion from the stored progress rather than add it
(or otherwise explicitly set the intended post-completion value). Keep repeat-tech
handling in mind; practical 2088 separately amended that family.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv arithmetic/bookkeeping defect introduced by
advc refactoring.


F083 / provisional KI#405 -- AdvCiv cached tech count increments when a tech is
REMOVED instead of decrementing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

INTRODUCTION
- AdvCiv practical 2169, commit 91ebe9eaa0fac82efca5ba70c7dfb8b968c51be8
  ("Tweak revolt chance penalties, nationality bar help"), advc.101, introduced
  cached CvTeam::m_iTechCount and getTechCount().
- The cache is initialized/serialized and used specifically to avoid repeatedly
  counting known techs.

BUG
In the non-repeat branch of CvTeam::setHasTech:

    m_abHasTech.set(eTech, bNewValue);
    m_iTechCount++;

The cache increments for BOTH bNewValue=true and bNewValue=false.

A transition true -> false should decrease the count by one. Instead it increases
by one, leaving the cache two higher than the real number of known techs after a
single removal.

NORMAL SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
Advanced Start explicitly supports removing a purchased/owned technology through
getAdvancedStartTechCost(..., false) and then:

    setHasTech(eTech, false, ...)

subject to dependency/unit/building checks. Thus this is not confined to hostile
or impossible calls. A remove/rebuy cycle can repeatedly increase the cache even
though the actual number of known technologies returns to its starting value.
Map-regeneration/initialization cleanup also contains false transitions and is an
additional cache-drift risk.

GAMEPLAY CONSUMERS
- CvCity::cultureStrength uses getTechCount()/numTechInfos to derive its era-like
  culture/revolt-strength factor.
- CvPlayerAI building valuation uses getTechCount() around the early-war pacing
  threshold (advc.131).
Therefore the stale cache can affect gameplay, not merely diagnostics.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Use a signed update corresponding to the state transition, e.g.

    m_iTechCount += (bNewValue ? 1 : -1);

with the existing early equality return guaranteeing that only real transitions
are counted. Preserve the existing special handling for repeatable techs.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv cached-state defect introduced with advc.101.

--------------------------------------------------------------

  reordered restoration now waits until m_eMaster is cleared. Contact/war
  alignment goes through meet / queueWar / triggerWars, and no second independent
  vassal-transition state loss was established in this pass.
- assignVassal/freeVassal deal plumbing is consistent with current master/vassal
  state; no new root promoted.
- changeProjectCount's project-art vector sizing is balanced. The project-art
  style chosen by an absorbed team may not be preserved through PA project-count
  maxing, but this remains cosmetic/visual state and does not meet the bug bar yet.
- VictoryCountdown / canLaunch remains normalized under F081, not split into
  multiple roots.
- Counterespionage setters, EspionagePointsAgainstTeam, ForceRevealedBonus and
  their ordinary update helpers did not expose an additional non-PA defect in

- processTech's map-centering flag is intentionally one-way-looking (also true for

  shape without stronger behavioral evidence.
- Circumnavigation correctly rejects non-wrapping maps in
  CvGame::circumnavigationAvailable before CvTeam::testCircumnavigated runs.
- Current serialization remains symmetric under the project's explicit current-

F084 / provisional KI#406 -- Advanced Start can refund a map-visible technology
while retaining its irreversible full-map reveal
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION
- TECH_SATELLITES has iAdvancedStartCost=100 and bMapVisible=1.
- CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartTechCost allows removal/refund of an owned tech when
  no still-owned dependent tech and no placed unit/building requires it.
- CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_TECH,...,false) then calls
  CvTeam::setHasTech(eTech,false,...) and refunds the points.
- Acquiring a bMapVisible tech enters CvTeam::setHasTech's owned-tech branch and
  calls GC.getMap().setRevealedPlots(getID(), true, true), permanently revealing
  all plots to the team.
- The false transition has no inverse map-unreveal operation. This is sensible in
  isolation because plot knowledge can also be legitimate from exploration,
  visibility, map trades, espionage and other sources; blindly unrevealing the
  world would destroy independent knowledge.

Therefore Advanced Start supports the sequence:

    buy Satellites -> reveal full world -> refund Satellites -> keep full world

The source technology and its points are gone while the irreversible benefit
remains.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
The same fundamental shape is present in the supplied Civ4CE/BtS control; this is
not introduced by recent SAS GameRecord plumbing.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Do not try to reverse per-plot knowledge. The conservative repair is to prohibit
Advanced Start removal/refund of a tech with bMapVisible once acquired (or more
generally mark irreversible tech effects nonrefundable).

A neighboring bMapCentering tech is also one-way in processTech, but current SAS
uses that as a UI/presentation capability and it does not independently meet the
bug bar established for the full-map reveal.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start irreversible-effect/refund defect.


F085 / provisional KI#407 -- Advanced Start tech refund does not roll back
currentEra, allowing later-era mechanics to persist without the corresponding
techs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATE TRANSITION
In CvTeam::setHasTech, acquiring any non-repeat tech with an era above a member's
current era does:

    if (kMember.getCurrentEra() < kTech.getEra())
        kMember.setCurrentEra((EraTypes)kTech.getEra());

There is no corresponding downward update on setHasTech(..., false). Search of the
current DLL shows that normal era advancement is otherwise not periodically
recomputed from the team's known-tech set; outside initialization/Python, this
acquisition path is what moves player era forward.

ADVANCED START REACHABILITY
Advanced Start explicitly permits reversible tech purchases. A player can buy a
later-era tech (after satisfying its prerequisites), thereby advance currentEra,
and then refund/remove that tech once no dependent owned content blocks removal.
The player remains in the higher era. With enough points the player can walk a
tech chain upward and refund it backward while retaining the highest reached era.

GAMEPLAY IMPACT
currentEra is not merely art/music state. Concrete current-SAS consumers include:
- CvUnit::getGreatWorkCulture multiplies Great Work culture by
  (owner.currentEra + 1).
- CvPlayer::doEvents uses the current era's EventChancePerTurn.
- CvPlayer::canBuild visibility/era tests depend on currentEra.
- Many AdvCiv/SAS AI valuation, military, worker, culture-victory and strategy
  heuristics depend directly on player currentEra.

Thus the Advanced Start refund can preserve real later-era mechanics after the
technology that caused the era transition has been removed.

ANCESTRY
The monotonic-era plus reversible-Advanced-Start-tech combination is inherited
from BtS/Civ4CE rather than introduced by SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Keep ordinary gameplay era progression monotonic. On an Advanced Start tech
removal, recompute each affected team member's era from the highest remaining
known non-repeat technology (bounded by the game start era), or equivalently
prevent removal when it would leave currentEra unsupported. Recomputing only in
the Advanced Start removal path avoids making normal post-start eras regress.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start cached/derived-state defect.


ADDITIONAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / STRENGTHENING
--------------------------------------------

- F081 was challenged for an ordinary post-launch reproduction independent of
  Permanent Alliances. CvPlayer::canCreate rejects victory-prerequisite projects
  whenever that victory already has a nonnegative countdown, including the
  bContinue=true queue path. Ordinary city production therefore cannot normally
  finish more spaceship parts after launch and re-enable canLaunch. F081 remains
  correctly scoped to project-count state changes that bypass normal construction,
  especially Permanent-Alliance project transfer.
- Repeat technologies use a separate acquisition-count path and are not evidence
  that F083's ordinary cached total-tech-count bug should be broadened.
- Tech-reveal bonus visibility, routes, trading counters, commerce flexibility,
  improvement yields, obsolete-building state and the ordinary signed processTech
  effects are generally reversed through iChange. No duplicate root was created
  merely because tech removal is uncommon.
- First-to-discover religion/free-tech/free-unit perks do not create an Advanced
  Start rebuy exploit through this path because Advanced Start acquisition calls
  setHasTech with bFirst=false.
- Current SpecialBuilding XML has no live TechPrereqAnyone value other than NONE,
  so no current-SAS global-special-building refund exploit was promoted.

F086 / provisional KI#408 -- Ancient-era Barbarian-contact threshold of zero
turns local contact into global contact and over-accelerates Barbarian research
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT CODE / REACHABILITY
CvTeam::isInContactWithBarbarians is the advc.302 gate used by
CvTeam::doBarbarianResearch when deciding how many civilization teams should
contribute to Barbarian free research.

During the early phase, before the city-contact fallback is enabled, it sets:

    int iUnitThresh = GC.getGame().getCurrentEra();

and is meant to skip map areas in which the civilization has too little unit
presence:

    if (!bCheckCity && countNumUnitsByArea(*pArea) < iUnitThresh)
        continue;

It then accepts contact when the same area contains more than iUnitThresh
Barbarian units.

In the Ancient era, currentEra is 0. Therefore:

    ownUnits < 0

can never be true. No area is filtered by the civilization's own presence. The
function consequently scans every area on the map, and any Barbarian unit
anywhere satisfies:

    barbarianUnits > 0

Thus, during the period when the function is specifically supposed to localize
contact through nearby units, one remote Barbarian unit can make every Ancient-
era civilization count as being in contact with Barbarians.

GAMEPLAY EFFECT
CvTeam::doBarbarianResearch counts civilization teams that both know a technology
and return true from isInContactWithBarbarians. F086 therefore inflates the
contact-weighted Barbarian research rate during the early phase, defeating the
geographic/contact distinction introduced for advc.302. The later fallback that
counts a fraction of all known civilizations does not make this harmless; the
whole point of the earlier branch is that actual contact should matter more.

ANCESTRY / INTENT CONTROL
The zero-threshold shape is inherited from AdvCiv's Barbarian-contact feature,
not introduced by current SAS. The source comment immediately above the threshold
already notes that perhaps a threshold of 1 would have the same effect, which is
consistent with the intended threshold being a positive unit-presence test rather
than zero in the Ancient era.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Give the unit threshold an explicit positive floor while retaining later-era
scaling, e.g. conceptually:

    iUnitThresh = max(1, currentEra)

Then the early phase requires at least some civilization presence in an area and
more than that threshold of Barbarian units, instead of globalizing contact in
era 0.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv Barbarian-research/contact-localization defect.


ADDITIONAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SECTIONS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
--------------------------------------------------------------

- AgentIterator::nextIndex was challenged because KI#207 established that it can
  be the wrong denominator when a caller applies an extra manual filter. That is
  not happening in the current CvTeam uses. MemberIter and TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE>
  either traverse exact cached sequences or account internally for predicate
  skips, so getCurrentEra, getHandicapType and both Barbarian-research alive-team
  divisors use valid counts. F086 is specifically the zero contact threshold.
- Permanent-Alliance field/state backfill did not establish another omitted live
  state beyond F078-F081. Tech and team-shared-building effects are deliberately
  cross-applied before player reassignment; project-making counts need their
  explicit merge because CvPlayer::setTeam does not transfer them automatically.
- The irreversible global Manhattan Project unlock is not a project-removal bug.
  Normal resetVictoryProgress only removes spaceship projects, while the
  Manhattan unlock is intentionally global/historical once completed.
- Cached war-enemy classification remains coherent when an existing wartime
  opponent changes vassal status: CvTeam::setVassal explicitly adjusts the
  cached vassal-war-enemy component on every team currently at war with it.
- Defensive-pact / peace-treaty first-list assumptions continue to be supported
  by the deal construction contract for those symmetric one-item trade deals.
- testCircumnavigated deliberately marks an already-complete very-early map as
  circumnavigated without awarding movement when the elapsed-turn gate is not
  met. Advanced Start full-map visibility can reach that policy, but this is an
  intentional early/scenario anti-reward shape, not promoted independently from
  F084.
- CvTeam::doTurn contains a source-authored "Known issue in networked
  multiplayer" around the advc.134a peace-offer staging workaround. It is being
  retained as an acknowledged limitation to investigate, not promoted as F087
  without a concrete reproducible state failure and repair contract.

C013-WIP05 -- CvTeam.cpp Permanent-Alliance espionage self-target checkpoint
===============================================================================

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE
--------------------
2026-08-25 08:50 light-source snapshot, practical 6252 / HEAD ad022a3f... plus
its bundled/reconciled audit album and staged KI#388-KI#390 implementation.

This checkpoint is append-only relative to C013-WIP04. No repository source was
modified.


F087 / provisional KI#409 -- Permanent Alliance redirects absorbed-team
espionage against the survivor into the survivor's self-target EP, polluting
K-Mod's total-unspent denominator and AI sea-spy targeting
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT CODE / REACHABILITY
CvTeam::shareItems merges the survivor A and absorbed team B's directed
espionage-point arrays by iterating every TeamTypes slot without excluding the
two constituent team IDs:

    setEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eLoopTeam,
        GET_TEAM(eTeam).getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eLoopTeam) +
        getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eLoopTeam));

For the iteration where eLoopTeam == A (the surviving team's own ID), this
becomes conceptually:

    A.EPvsA = B.EPvsA + A.EPvsA

B.EPvsA is perfectly ordinary pre-alliance espionage accumulated against the
future ally. Once B's players are reassigned to team A, however, those points
have no valid external target. They have instead been stored as A's espionage
against itself.

The analogous A->B constituent slot is also obsolete after B disappears and
should not become meaningful merged espionage. Outsider-target slots are the
ones that should be combined.

SELF EP IS NOT DEAD STATE
K-Mod's CvTeam::getTotalUnspentEspionage sums:

    for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
        iTotal += getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(it->getID());

TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> is backed directly by CvAgents::CIV_ALIVE, whose cache
contains every alive non-Barbarian civilization team. There is no relation
predicate excluding the iterating team; AgentPredicates explicitly distinguishes
NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS / OTHER_KNOWN_TO when self is supposed to be excluded. Thus A's
new A->A EP is included in getTotalUnspentEspionage.

GAMEPLAY EFFECT
CvUnitAI::AI_specialSeaTransportSpy uses getTotalUnspentEspionage as the
denominator when measuring how much of the team's espionage stock is aimed at
each real target:

    iValue = 1000 * EPvsTarget / max(1, iTotalPoints);

For example, suppose before the alliance:

    A has 1000 EP against outsider C
    B has 1000 EP against A

After B is absorbed, the current merge leaves A with 1000 EP against C plus
1000 EP against itself. A's real C target therefore falls from a 100% share of
its useful unspent EP to only 50% in AI_specialSeaTransportSpy, despite no real
espionage having been redirected away from C. This depresses the base values used
to select and route sea-transported spies and can alter whether/where those
missions are pursued. SASGameRecord's total-unspent value is contaminated too.

Other espionage AI code often uses explicit OTHER/NOT_SAME team iterators and is
therefore protected; that is a useful control and confirms that the unfiltered
K-Mod total is semantically intended to represent useful rival-target EP rather
than self-target residue.

ANCESTRY
The bad constituent-slot merge is inherited. Vanilla/Civ4CE's shareItems loops
all MAX_TEAMS too and uses max rather than sum, so B->A EP can already be written
into A->A. Kek-Mod/AdvCiv practical 1400 ([dlph.26], "Permanent alliance
bugfixes and adjustments") changed espionage merging from max to sum but retained
the same missing constituent-team exclusion. Current AdvCiv/SAS inherits that
shape.

REPAIR DIRECTION
During Permanent-Alliance espionage merging:

1. Sum the two constituent teams' EP only for genuine outsider targets.
2. Discard/clear the survivor-self and absorbed-team target slots; espionage
   previously spent by A against B or B against A cannot remain useful after the
   two teams become one.
3. As defensive hardening, make getTotalUnspentEspionage explicitly exclude the
   team's own ID (e.g. a NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS iterator), so stale/corrupt self-target
   EP can never distort AI denominators again.

Do not redistribute mutual constituent espionage to unrelated rivals; there is no
source-supported target for such a transfer.

Classification: inherited BtS/K-Mod Permanent-Alliance espionage-state defect
with current K-Mod AI gameplay consequence.


ADDITIONAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SECTIONS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
--------------------------------------------------------------

- The F087 effect is not caused by AgentIterator counting semantics. The
  CvAgents::CIV_ALIVE cache itself includes the survivor team; getTotalUnspent
  simply chooses an unfiltered iterator. This is distinct from the earlier
  KI#207 nextIndex/manual-filter bug.
- Outsider -> merged-team espionage is separately combined later in addTeam and
  is directionally correct. F087 concerns the constituent A/B target slots in
  the survivor's own espionage array, not the outsider reverse merge.
- The absorbed-team target slot A->B becomes irrelevant once B is dead and is
  normally excluded from alive-team totals; the harmful slot is specifically
  B->A being redirected into survivor A->A. Clearing both constituent slots is
  nevertheless the clean merge invariant.

F088 / provisional KI#410 -- Advanced Start tech refunds validate only later
techs and the acting player's units/buildings, allowing live team/map
infrastructure dependencies to survive after their prerequisite tech is sold
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT CODE / REACHABILITY
CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_TECH) obtains the refund
price from getAdvancedStartTechCost(eTech, false), then removes the technology
from the entire team through:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).setHasTech(eTech, false, getID(), false, false);

and refunds the Advanced Start points.

The removal-side validator in CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartTechCost does check:

1. later team technologies that require eTech;
2. units belonging to *this player* whose unit definition requires eTech;
3. buildings in *this player's* cities whose building definition requires eTech.

Two live dependency classes are omitted.

A. OWNED IMPROVEMENTS / ROUTES
------------------------------
The validator never scans map infrastructure already purchased through the
technology. The Advanced Start add-cost helpers do enforce the build technology
when the infrastructure is placed, but removing the technology later does not
remove the resulting improvement/route and does not retroactively invalidate its
ordinary plot yield/movement effect.

Current SAS gives simple reachable examples:

- TECH_AGRICULTURE has an Advanced Start cost and enables BUILD_FARM and
  BUILD_PLANTATION. Farms/Plantations themselves have Advanced Start costs.
  Agriculture can therefore be bought, the infrastructure purchased, and the
  technology refunded while the placed infrastructure remains.
- TECH_THE_WHEEL enables BUILD_ROAD. A Road can be purchased and then the tech
  refunded while the physical route remains.
- Current SAS places BUILD_RAILROAD behind TECH_STEAM_POWER. Railroad likewise
  has an Advanced Start cost, so the same buy-place-refund sequence exists there.

Technology loss can remove some *technology-gated* secondary effects (for
example bonus revelation/connectivity through the normal team-tech machinery),
but it does not erase the infrastructure's own persistent map state and ordinary
route/improvement benefits. Thus the refund can retain value whose prerequisite
was paid only temporarily.

B. TEAMMATE UNIT / BUILDING DEPENDENCIES
----------------------------------------
Technology ownership is team-wide, but the unit/building validation uses only
FOR_EACH_UNIT(..., *this) and FOR_EACH_CITY(..., *this) for the player pressing
Refund. It never iterates the other members of that team.

Therefore, on a multi-player team, player B can satisfy the local refund check
while teammate A still owns units/buildings that require eTech; the subsequent
setHasTech(false) removes the technology from the whole team anyway. This is the
same incomplete dependency-validation root, not a separate finding.

CONTROL / ANCESTRY
------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same removal validator shape. The supplied
Civ4CE/BtS control likewise checks dependent team techs followed by the acting
player's units/cities and does not cover existing routes/improvements or the
other team members. This is therefore an inherited BtS Advanced Start contract
hole, not a SAS regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Keep the repair at the Advanced Start refund-validation boundary rather than
trying to destroy objects after team technology has already been removed:

1. For bAdd == false, validate unit/building dependencies across *all* living
   members of the team, because the state being removed is team-wide.
2. Reject removal while an owned improvement or route whose construction/build
   requires eTech remains on the map (using the actual build/prerequisite
   relationship rather than a hard-coded improvement/route list).
3. Preserve the existing later-tech dependency checks.

This also composes naturally with F084/F085: Advanced Start technology removal
needs to be treated as a reversible transaction only when all persistent state
that depends on that technology can remain internally valid.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start dependency/refund-validation defect.


F089 / provisional KI#411 -- Permanent Alliance fails to merge K-Mod hasSeen
historical civilization-identity knowledge, so absorbed players can forget a
civilization identity they knew before joining the surviving team
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT STATE / CONTRACT
------------------------
K-Mod practical 728 (77a9b8d554...) introduced CvTeam::m_abHasSeen. Its commit
message explicitly describes this as broader than first contact: it tracks teams
that have "been seen" and can become true through "map trading and things like
that." The flag is deliberately historical/persistent and is used by AdvCiv/K-Mod
to decide whether a civilization's leader/civilization identity and player color
may be shown to an observer.

Current sources set hasSeen when, among other things:

- a team actually meets another team (makeHasMet/makeHasSeen);
- a revealed plot exposes an owner (CvPlot::setRevealedOwner);
- a city becomes revealed (CvCity::setRevealed).

PERMANENT-ALLIANCE OMISSION
---------------------------
CvTeam::addTeam unions actual first-contact state by calling meet for contacts
known to either constituent team, and later transfers revealed plot/city data.
However, addTeam/shareItems/shareCounters never union m_abHasSeen itself.

Current-map transfer often masks this omission: if the absorbed team currently
has a revealed city or a revealed owner that still matches the plot's current
owner, copying that information causes the survivor to call makeHasSeen again.
But hasSeen is historical precisely because that current evidence need not still
exist.

CONCRETE LOSS CASE
------------------
A normal sequence can therefore be:

1. Team B learns civilization C's identity without first contact, e.g. through
   map/city information; B.hasSeen(C) becomes true.
2. The particular city/territory through which C was identified later changes
   owner (or otherwise no longer supplies current C-owned revealed evidence),
   while C remains alive elsewhere and B still correctly retains historical
   hasSeen(C).
3. B forms a Permanent Alliance into surviving team A, which has never seen/met
   C.
4. The transferred current map can identify the *current* owner, but there is no
   code transferring historical B.hasSeen(C).
5. B's players are reassigned to team A. Their identity-visibility checks now
   consult A.hasSeen(C), which remains false. The former B player can therefore
   have C's name/civilization/color concealed again despite having known it
   immediately before the alliance.

The state loss is especially clear because the absorbed CvTeam object is no
longer used after the merge; leaving the bit only on B is equivalent to deleting
that historical knowledge.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
The omission follows K-Mod's addition of m_abHasSeen: the K-Mod practical-728
change introduced/reset/serialized the field and hooked it to reveal/contact
paths, while the inherited Permanent-Alliance merger was not taught to combine
it. Current base AdvCiv 1.14 still has no hasSeen union in addTeam/shareItems or
shareCounters. Vanilla Civ4CE/BtS predates this K-Mod field and therefore cannot
serve as a field-level control.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
During Permanent Alliance, union historical identity knowledge explicitly:

    if (absorbed.isHasSeen(eOther))
        survivor.makeHasSeen(eOther);

for relevant team IDs (and, if the disappearing team's state is needed during
pre-reassignment processing, preserve the symmetric temporary direction as
appropriate). Do not rely on current revealed ownership to reconstruct a
historical flag; that loses exactly the cases m_abHasSeen was introduced to
remember.

Classification: inherited K-Mod Permanent-Alliance state-merge omission with
observer-facing identity regression.


ADDITIONAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SECTIONS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
--------------------------------------------------------------

- A mechanical current-schema serialization matrix compared all 72 live CvTeam
  data members declared in the persistent/transient state block against reset,
  read and write. Every persistent member has symmetric read/write handling.
  The only two members intentionally absent from serialization are advc.134a's
  m_eOfferingPeace and m_iPeaceOfferStage; both are transient EXE diplomacy-
  handshake state reset to NO_TEAM/0 rather than durable game state. No hidden
  save/load root was found there.
- The advc.134a source comment still acknowledges a networked-multiplayer peace-
  offer limitation, but no deterministic state failure + repair contract has yet
  been established. It remains unpromoted rather than turning an author warning
  into an unsupported finding.
- Defensive Pact/Open Borders/peace-treaty deal paths that look one-sided locally
  are constructed as symmetric/dual deal data where their callers require that
  contract; no additional relation-state root was established from those paths.
- hasSeen should *not* be inferred solely from hasMet: K-Mod intentionally made
  it broader than contact. Conversely, current-map transfer can legitimately
  re-create many hasSeen bits, which is why F089 is specifically about the
  historical residue that current revealed ownership cannot reconstruct.

F090 / provisional KI#412 -- AdvCiv reparations announcements resolve
player-local city IDs through the giving team's leader, so a city ceded by a
nonleader teammate can be misnamed or omitted
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PAYLOAD CONTRACT
----------------
TRADE_CITIES stores the city ID belonging to the specific player who owns and
cedes the city. City IDs are player-local, not team-global. CvDeal::startTrade
uses the correct contract when executing a city trade:

    kFromPlayer.getCity(trade.m_iData)

where kFromPlayer is the actual player on the giving side of that deal item.

ADVCIV ANNOUNCEMENT MISMATCH
----------------------------
The advc.039 reparations-announcement path discards that player identity before
formatting the peace terms. CvTeam::tradeItemString receives only the giving
TeamTypes and, for TRADE_CITIES, resolves the same numeric city ID through:

    GET_PLAYER(kFrom.getLeaderID()).getCity(iData)

That is only correct if the giving player is the team leader. After a Permanent
Alliance, one team can contain several players with independent city-ID
namespaces, so identical numeric city IDs can refer to entirely different
cities.

CONCRETE REACHABLE CASE
-----------------------
1. Players A and B are members of the same team after a Permanent Alliance; A is
   the team's leader.
2. B participates in a later peace deal and cedes B's city ID 0.
3. A also owns its own unrelated city ID 0.
4. CvDeal executes the item correctly through B and transfers B's city.
5. The advc.039 announcement formatter later resolves numeric ID 0 through team
   leader A and can announce A's different city as the reparations city.
6. If A has no city with that local ID, the lookup fails and the city term can
   disappear from the formatted reparations instead.

The deal path is not leader-only: CvDeal participants are PlayerTypes, and the
peace-treaty/trade machinery remains reachable for individual members of a
multi-player team. Therefore this is not merely a malformed synthetic payload.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
The mismatch is already present in the AdvCiv advc.039 implementation. The
ordinary CvDeal execution path provides the clean control because it retains the
specific giving player and resolves TRADE_CITIES correctly from that player's
city table.

The neighboring reparations payloads do not share this defect:
- technologies, civics and religions use global info IDs;
- maps are naturally team-level;
- the relevant target/team arguments are otherwise supplied consistently.
City IDs are exceptional because they are allocated independently per player.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not try to recover the city owner by scanning members of the giving team:
two teammates can legitimately own the same numeric city ID. Preserve the actual
reparations-giving PlayerTypes from CvDeal through the announcement path and use
that player when formatting TRADE_CITIES. TeamTypes can remain sufficient for
team-global trade-item kinds.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv advc.039 UI/reporting payload-identity defect.


ADDITIONAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SECTIONS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
--------------------------------------------------------------

- Other trade-item formatting cases around tradeItemString were checked for the
  same player-vs-team identity loss. No comparable mismatch was established:
  their IDs are global or intentionally team-level.
- The BBAI Defensive Pact behavior-2 source warning remains unpromoted. Current
  SAS config uses behavior 0, and the stale warning alone is not enough evidence
  for a current reachable F091 without a deterministic failure + repair.
- advc.134a's networked-multiplayer peace-offer warning likewise remains an
  acknowledged source limitation rather than an audit root until a precise
  reachable state failure can be demonstrated.

F091 / provisional KI#413 -- AdvCiv forced-peace duration helper assumes a
peace treaty is the first item of the first deal list, so valid reparations
peace can be reported as having zero turns remaining
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
CvTeam::turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining is meant to recover the remaining lifetime
of a mandatory peace treaty from live CvDeal objects. After confirming that the
team-level isForcePeace flag is active, it scans deals between the relevant
master teams but recognizes a treaty only when:

    d->getLengthFirst() > 0 &&
    d->getFirstList().head()->m_data.m_eItemType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY

This makes physical list side and list order part of a logical team-level
forced-peace query.

NORMAL REACHABLE COUNTEREXAMPLE
-------------------------------
AdvCiv itself deliberately places peace treaties at the bottom of offer lists.
CvPlayer::updateTradeList removes/re-appends peacetime treaty items specifically
so that they are at the bottom for the diplomacy Python UI.

The ordinary AI peace/reparations path also constructs lists in which a giving
side may contain, for example:

    TRADE_GOLD / TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES / TRADE_CITIES ... TRADE_PEACE_TREATY

and then ensures the other side contains a treaty too before either opening the
human diplomacy popup or calling CvGame::implementDeal for AI-AI peace.
Consequently the resulting deal can have fully symmetric, valid forced peace
while the head of the first list is a reparations item rather than the treaty.

In that state isForcePeace(eOther) is true, but
turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining(eOther) ignores the live treaty and returns 0.

GAMEPLAY / AI CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------
The helper is not cosmetic. UWAI uses the remaining duration to:
- delay concluding war preparations while more than three treaty turns remain;
- decide whether a switch to an alternative target can fit before forced peace
  ends;
- reduce war-preparation drive in proportion to the treaty time remaining.
CvPlayerAI also uses the helper to gate help/tribute diplomatic actions.

Returning zero therefore lets AI planning and diplomacy behave as though
mandatory peace has already expired even though CvTeam::canDeclareWar still
correctly blocks an actual declaration until the treaty ends.

ANCESTRY
--------
The list-head assumption is present in the advc.104 introduction of
turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining at AdvCiv practical 1253 / f6ff6a182f.... A later
null/empty-list guard did not change the physical first-list/head requirement.
This is therefore an inherited AdvCiv helper defect rather than an SAS
regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Search both trade lists of each matching deal and recognize
TRADE_PEACE_TREATY anywhere in either list. The logical duration query should
not depend on which participant physically stores the treaty item or on its
position among reparations/annual items.

Do not merely move peace treaties to the head: AdvCiv intentionally keeps some
trade UI lists ordered with the treaty at the bottom, and the robust contract is
that the helper locate the item rather than impose UI list order on deal state.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv advc.104 forced-peace duration / deal-layout
contract defect.


ADDITIONAL CONTROLS / OPEN NEIGHBOR
-----------------------------------

- The cached major/minor/vassal war-count audit did not produce a minor-status
  sibling: CvInitCore explicitly treats changing minor-civ status after game
  start as unsupported, while setVassal already repairs the supported live
  vassal reclassification.
- CvPlayer::resetDualDeal also assumes first-list storage, but unlike F091 it
  scans the whole first list rather than only the head. Normal symmetric peace
  construction therefore still finds the treaty there. A separate defect would
  require proving a final live one-sided-treaty representation, so this remains
  under challenge rather than being promoted from the source comment alone.
- K-Mod/AdvCiv deliberately uses one-sided peace-treaty items transiently while
  counter-proposing because the EXE dislikes adding the item to both sides.
  Whether every accepted route later symmetrizes the team-level forced-peace
  state is still being traced. F091 does not depend on this unresolved question.

F092 / provisional KI#414 -- AdvCiv's optimized Tech Share first-contact scan
uses the reverse directional hasMet relation before it is initialized, making
The Internet's free-tech grant depend on which team initiates contact
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
CvTeam::meet establishes contact by calling makeHasMet in sequence:

    makeHasMet(eTeam, ...);
    GET_TEAM(eTeam).makeHasMet(getID(), ...);

Each makeHasMet sets only its own directional has-met turn and immediately calls
updateTechShare(). Current updateTechShare iterates:

    TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,OTHER_KNOWN_TO> itOther(getID())

but AgentIterator's OTHER_KNOWN_TO predicate is deliberately directional in the
opposite direction:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam(kAgent)).isHasMet(m_eTeam)

Thus the first team's Tech Share scan runs before the second team has recorded
that it knows the first team. The newly encountered team is absent from that
scan even though the first team has already set its own hasMet(other) state.
The second team's makeHasMet then gets the reciprocal state and scans normally.

CURRENT-SAS REPRODUCTION
------------------------
The current XML has one Tech Share source, PROJECT_THE_INTERNET, with
<iTechShare>2</iTechShare> and <iMaxGlobalInstances>1</iMaxGlobalInstances>.
That makes a clean asymmetric reproduction:

- A owns The Internet and already knows C.
- C and newly encountered B both know technology X; A does not.
- B does not own The Internet (the project is globally unique).
- Contact with B should raise A's known holders of X from one player to two and
  immediately grant X.

If the contact path calls A.meet(B), A is processed first. Its updateTechShare
scan sees C but cannot yet see B through OTHER_KNOWN_TO, so it remains at 1/2
and X is not granted. B is processed second but has no Tech Share capability and
cannot compensate.

If the same first contact is reached with B.meet(A), B is processed first and A
second. By the time A scans, B's reciprocal has-met state exists, so A sees both
B and C and correctly receives X.

Both caller orientations occur naturally. Unit movement can call the observing
team's meet(movingTeam), while plot/territory visibility can call the owning
team's meet(viewingTeam). There is no invariant that the Internet owner is
always second.

WHY THE LOSS CAN PERSIST
------------------------
Tech Share updates are event-driven, not continuously recomputed. They run on
first contact, on Tech Share count changes, and when a team acquires a
technology (which asks other teams to update that particular tech). In the
reproduction B already had X before first contact, and B cannot build a second
Internet. Therefore no same-contact fallback necessarily rechecks X for A.
The missed grant can persist until some unrelated later event causes another
full Tech Share update.

ANCESTRY
--------
Vanilla BtS updateTechShare scans alive teams and checks the receiving team's own
relation:

    if (isHasMet((TeamTypes)iI))

By the time makeHasMet calls updateTechShare, that receiving-side relation has
already been set, so vanilla includes the newly met team.

AdvCiv practical 1837 / 74de2f9c0f... optimized the scan to
TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,KNOWN_TO>. AgentIterator's KNOWN_TO relation uses the reverse
other.isHasMet(this) direction. Practical 1842 later changed KNOWN_TO to
OTHER_KNOWN_TO only to exclude self; it retained the same directional predicate
and therefore the ordering defect. Current SAS inherits it.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Prefer establishing both reciprocal has-met states before evaluating Tech Share.
A causal repair is to remove updateTechShare() from makeHasMet and, in meet,
call updateTechShare() for both teams only after both makeHasMet calls have
finished. This also gives Tech Share the natural logical contract: first make
contact symmetric, then evaluate effects that depend on contact.

Alternatively, updateTechShare could explicitly iterate from the receiving
team's own isHasMet relation, but keeping dependent updates after reciprocal
contact is less fragile and avoids similar ordering assumptions later.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv practical-1837 first-contact / AgentIterator
relation-direction regression.
